# Test USB boot priority control via LPS using bootOrderConfig (usb/nousb)
# This test verifies that LPS can control USB boot order on a per-VM basis
#
# PREREQUISITES:
# ==============
# This test requires a USB disk image (Debian) attached to EVE's QEMU.
# Before running this test, you must set up the USB disk using one of these methods:
#
# Method 1: Use the setup script (RECOMMENDED)
#   1. Run: EDEN=./eden ./tests/eclient/usb-boot-setup.sh
#   2. Configure port forwarding:
#      EDEN=./eden ./tests/eclient/eden+ports.sh 8027:8027 8028:8028 8029:8029 8030:8030 8031:8031
#   3. Then run: ./eden setup && ./eden start && ./eden eve onboard
#   4. Finally: ./eden test tests/eclient -v debug -e usb_boot_priority
#
# Method 2: Manual configuration
#   1. Download Debian cloud image:
#      curl -L -o /tmp/debian.raw https://cloud.debian.org/images/cloud/bookworm/latest/debian-12-nocloud-amd64.raw
#   2. Configure Eden with USB disk:
#      ./eden config add default --eve-usb-disks="/tmp/debian.raw"
#   3. Configure port forwarding (ports 8027-8031 for test VM SSH):
#      EDEN=./eden ./tests/eclient/eden+ports.sh 8027:8027 8028:8028 8029:8029 8030:8030 8031:8031
#   4. Setup and start Eden: ./eden setup && ./eden start && ./eden eve onboard
#   5. Run test: ./eden test tests/eclient -v debug -e usb_boot_priority
#
# Method 3: Run via workflow (used in GH Actions)
#   The usb-boot.tests.txt workflow handles port forwarding automatically.
#   Run: ./eden test ./tests/workflow -s usb-boot.tests.txt -v debug
#   Note: Requires usb-boot-setup.sh to be run first (done by setup-environment action in CI)
#
# What this test verifies:
# The fw_cfg "opt/eve.bootorder" tells OVMF (UEFI firmware) how to order boot devices.
# - "usb": Prioritize USB devices in boot order -> VM boots from USB disk (Debian)
# - "nousb": Deprioritize USB devices in boot order -> VM boots from main drive (Ubuntu)
# - "" or unset: Default boot order (determined by FML resolution config)
#
# Test cases:
#
# Boot Order Tests (1-6):
#   TC1: Custom resolution, no fw_cfg -> HDD boot (Ubuntu) - default boot order
#   TC2: No resolution, no fw_cfg -> USB boot (Debian) - OVMF default prefers USB
#   TC3: Custom resolution, fw_cfg="usb" -> USB boot (Debian) - fw_cfg overrides
#   TC4: No resolution, fw_cfg="usb" -> USB boot (Debian) - fw_cfg confirms USB priority
#   TC5: Custom resolution, fw_cfg="nousb" -> HDD boot (Ubuntu) - fw_cfg deprioritizes USB
#   TC6: No resolution, fw_cfg="nousb" -> HDD boot (Ubuntu) - fw_cfg overrides OVMF default
#
# Multi-VM Test (7):
#   TC7: Per-VM USB boot control with different settings for each VM
#
# LPS Config Parsing Tests (8-9):
#   TC8: UUID-only config (no displayname) -> EVE matches by UUID
#   TC9: Displayname-only config (no UUID) -> EVE matches by displayname
#
# LPS Address Change Test (10):
#   TC10: Verify EVE re-fetches config when LPS address changes (pause/resume)
#
# HTTP Status Code Tests (11-13):
#   TC11: HTTP 200/201 - Normal config response
#   TC12: HTTP 204 - No content (config unchanged), also 200 with same content
#   TC13: HTTP 404 - Not found (triggers throttling and recovery)
#
# Config Reset Tests (14-16):
#   TC14: Reset by removing app from config
#   TC15: Reset by setting usb_boot="" explicitly
#   TC16: Reset ALL apps by sending empty config
#
# Persistence Test (17):
#   TC17: Verify config persists across EVE reboot
#
# The USB disk contains Debian, the main drive contains Ubuntu cloud image.
# We verify the correct OS booted by checking console output for "Debian" vs "Ubuntu".
#
# KNOWN LIMITATION: When Debian boots from USB, the VM may crash shortly after boot
# because EVE's usbmanager may disconnect the USB device. The test uses polling
# to catch the brief RUNNING state and verify boot OS from console logs.
#
# NOTE: The USB disk (Debian) is attached via --adapters USB<bus>:<port> passthrough.
# The bootOrderConfig field in LPS API accepts: "", "usb", or "nousb".

{{define "port"}}8027{{end}}
{{define "vm_port"}}8028{{end}}
{{define "token"}}server_token_usb_boot_test{{end}}
{{define "appbootconfig_file"}}/mnt/appbootconfig{{end}}
{{define "network"}}n1{{end}}
{{define "ssh"}}ssh -q -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o PasswordAuthentication=no -i {{EdenConfig "eden.tests"}}/eclient/image/cert/id_rsa root@FWD_IP -p FWD_PORT{{end}}
{{define "eclient_image"}}docker://nikolayzededa/eden-eclient:1.0.20{{end}}
{{define "test_vm"}}test-usb-boot-vm{{end}}
{{define "test_vm_2"}}test-usb-boot-vm-2{{end}}

[!exec:bash] stop
[!exec:sleep] stop
[!exec:ssh] stop
[!exec:chmod] stop
[!exec:jq] stop

exec chmod 600 {{EdenConfig "eden.tests"}}/eclient/image/cert/id_rsa


message 'Resetting of EVE'
eden eve reset
exec sleep 30

# Create n1 network
eden -t 1m network create 10.11.12.0/24 -n {{template "network"}}
test eden.network.test -test.v -timewait 2m ACTIVATED {{template "network"}}

# Deploy local-manager (LPS simulator)
eden pod deploy -n local-manager --memory=512MB {{template "eclient_image"}} -p {{template "port"}}:22 --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING local-manager

# Wait for ssh access to local-manager
exec -t 5m bash wait-ssh.sh {{template "port"}}

# Start local manager application with VM config support
exec -t 1m bash local-manager-start.sh

# Obtain local-manager IP address
exec -t 2m bash get-app-ip.sh local-manager
source .env

# Configure local server
eden controller edge-node update --device profile_server_token={{template "token"}}
eden controller edge-node update --device local_profile_server=$app_ip:8888

# ============================================================================
# STEP 0: Verify LPS endpoint is working
# ============================================================================
message 'STEP 0: Verify LPS boot config endpoint is accessible'
exec -t 2m bash verify-lps-endpoint.sh
! stdout 'ENDPOINT_ERROR'
stdout 'LPS endpoint verified'

# Detect USB harddrive on EVE dynamically
# The USB topology can change, so we detect it at runtime
message 'Detecting USB harddrive on EVE for passthrough'
exec -t 1m bash detect-usb-harddrive.sh
source .env
stdout 'USB_ADAPTER='


# ============================================================================
# TC1: Custom resolution, no fw_cfg -> HDD boot (Ubuntu)
# This is the default state: FML resolution set, no bootOrderConfig
# OVMF sees resolution config and boots from HDD
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC1: Custom resolution + no fw_cfg -> Ubuntu (HDD boot) ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Set FML resolution (this affects default boot order in OVMF)
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=1024x768

# Wait for EVE to pick up the resolution setting
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply FML resolution setting...'
exec -t 2m bash wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh 1024x768

# Deploy test VM with USB passthrough
message 'Deploying test VM with OVMF and USB passthrough'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Record timestamp for log filtering
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify no fw_cfg is set (bootOrderConfig is empty)
message 'TC1a: Verify NO fw_cfg in hypervisor config (no bootOrderConfig set)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid none
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: not set'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (HDD boot due to resolution)
message 'TC1b: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - default with resolution'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC1 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC2: No resolution, no fw_cfg -> USB boot (Debian)
# When no resolution is set, OVMF defaults to USB boot priority
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC2: No resolution + no fw_cfg -> Debian (USB boot) ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Remove FML resolution
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=

# Wait for EVE to pick up the resolution change
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply FML resolution removal...'
exec -t 2m bash wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh ""

# Redeploy VM for new test scenario (delete and deploy again)
message 'Redeploying VM for test case 2'
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
# USB boot VM may crash - use custom polling (5m timeout to match script's internal timeout)
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID (may have changed after redeploy)
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Record timestamp before checking logs
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify no fw_cfg is still set
message 'TC2a: Verify NO fw_cfg in hypervisor config'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid none
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: not set'

# Verify Debian boots (USB boot - OVMF default without resolution)
message 'TC2b: Verify VM boots from USB (Debian) - OVMF default without resolution'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC2 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC3: Custom resolution + fw_cfg="usb" -> USB boot (Debian)
# fw_cfg="usb" overrides the resolution setting
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC3: Custom resolution + fw_cfg=usb -> Debian (USB boot) ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Re-enable resolution
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=1024x768

# Wait for EVE to pick up the resolution change
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply FML resolution setting...'
exec -t 2m bash wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh 1024x768

# Redeploy VM for new test scenario
message 'Redeploying VM for test case 3'
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID (may have changed after redeploy)
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Set bootOrderConfig=usb via LPS
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify EVE received the config
message 'TC3a: Verify EVE received bootOrderConfig=usb'
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Restart VM to apply fw_cfg (restart is appropriate here - applying a setting)
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp before checking logs
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg=usb is in hypervisor config
message 'TC3b: Verify fw_cfg=usb in hypervisor config'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Check OVMF debug/console output
message 'TC3c: Check OVMF EVE-BOOT messages'
exec -t 2m bash check-ovmf-debug-v2.sh $vm_uuid
stdout '=== OVMF debug check complete ==='

# Verify EVE-BOOT console messages
message 'TC3d: Verify EVE-BOOT messages in console'
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-boot-console-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} usb
stdout 'EVE-BOOT'

# Verify Debian boots (USB boot - fw_cfg overrides resolution)
message 'TC3e: Verify VM boots from USB (Debian) - fw_cfg=usb overrides resolution'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC3 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC4: No resolution + fw_cfg="usb" -> USB boot (Debian)
# fw_cfg="usb" confirms USB priority (same as OVMF default)
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC4: No resolution + fw_cfg=usb -> Debian (USB boot) ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Remove resolution
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=

# Wait for EVE to pick up the resolution removal
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply FML resolution removal...'
exec -t 2m bash wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh ""

# Redeploy VM for new test scenario
message 'Redeploying VM for test case 4'
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID (may have changed after redeploy)
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Set bootOrderConfig=usb via LPS
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Restart VM to apply fw_cfg (restart is appropriate here - applying a setting)
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp before checking logs

# Verify fw_cfg=usb still present

stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Verify Debian boots
message 'TC4b: Verify VM boots from USB (Debian)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC4 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC5: Custom resolution + fw_cfg="nousb" -> HDD boot (Ubuntu)
# fw_cfg="nousb" explicitly deprioritizes USB
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC5: Custom resolution + fw_cfg=nousb -> Ubuntu (HDD boot) ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Re-enable resolution
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=1024x768

# Wait for EVE to pick up the resolution change
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply FML resolution setting...'
exec -t 2m bash wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh 1024x768

# Redeploy VM for new test scenario
message 'Redeploying VM for test case 5'
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID (may have changed after redeploy)
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Set bootOrderConfig=nousb via LPS
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid nousb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify EVE received the config
message 'TC5a: Verify EVE received bootOrderConfig=nousb'
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Restart VM to apply fw_cfg (restart is appropriate here - applying a setting)
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp before checking logs
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg=nousb in hypervisor config
message 'TC5b: Verify fw_cfg=nousb in hypervisor config'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (HDD boot - nousb deprioritizes USB)
message 'TC5c: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - nousb deprioritizes USB'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC5 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC6: No resolution + fw_cfg="nousb" -> HDD boot (Ubuntu)
# fw_cfg="nousb" overrides OVMF default USB preference
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC6: No resolution + fw_cfg=nousb -> Ubuntu (HDD boot) ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Remove resolution
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=

# Wait for EVE to pick up the resolution removal
message 'Waiting for EVE to apply FML resolution removal...'
exec -t 2m bash wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh ""

# Redeploy VM for new test scenario
message 'Redeploying VM for test case 6'
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID (may have changed after redeploy)
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Set bootOrderConfig=nousb via LPS
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid nousb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Restart VM to apply fw_cfg (restart is appropriate here - applying a setting)
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Record timestamp before checking logs
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg=nousb persists
message 'TC6a: Verify fw_cfg=nousb persists'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Verify Ubuntu boots (HDD boot - nousb overrides OVMF default)
message 'TC6b: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) - nousb overrides OVMF USB default'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'
message '=== TC6 PASSED ==='


# ============================================================================
# TC7: Multi-VM - Per-VM USB boot control with different settings
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC7: Per-VM USB boot control ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Redeploy first VM fresh for multi-VM test
message 'Redeploying VM1 for multi-VM test'
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Deploy second VM (no USB passthrough - will always boot from HDD)
message 'Deploying second test VM'
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm_2"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=2 --fml https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm_2"}}

# Get both VM UUIDs using direct variable save to avoid intermediate variable issues
exec bash get-vm-uuid-as.sh {{template "test_vm"}} vm1_uuid
exec bash get-vm-uuid-as.sh {{template "test_vm_2"}} vm2_uuid
source .env

# Set different boot orders: VM1=usb, VM2=nousb
message 'Setting VM1=usb, VM2=nousb'
exec -t 2m bash set-multi-vm-boot-order.sh $vm1_uuid usb $vm2_uuid nousb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Restart both VMs
message 'Restarting both VMs'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm_2"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm_2"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm_2"}}
# VM2 can wait normally, VM1 (USB boot) needs custom polling
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm_2"}}
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

# Verify per-VM fw_cfg settings
message 'TC7a: Verify VM1 has fw_cfg=usb'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm1_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

message 'TC7b: Verify VM2 has fw_cfg=nousb'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm2_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Record timestamp before checking logs
exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify correct OS boots on each VM
message 'TC7c: Verify VM1 boots Debian (USB)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

message 'TC7d: Verify VM2 boots Ubuntu (HDD)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm_2"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Clean up VM2 before UUID-only test
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm_2"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm_2"}}

message '=== TC7 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC8: LPS Parsing - UUID-only config (no displayname)
# EVE should be able to match VM by UUID alone
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC8: Config with UUID only (no displayname) ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Redeploy VM fresh for this test
message 'Redeploying VM for UUID-only parsing test'
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Get test VM UUID
exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# Set bootOrderConfig=usb via LPS using UUID only (no displayname field)
message 'Setting bootOrderConfig using UUID only (no displayname)'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order-uuid-only.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify EVE received and processed the config
message 'TC8a: Verify EVE received UUID-only config'
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Restart VM to apply fw_cfg
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}

# TC10: LPS Address Change - Verify EVE re-fetches config when LPS address changes
# This tests the pause/resume mechanism in LocalCmdAgent.UpdateLpsConfig()
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC10: LPS address change triggers config re-fetch ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Ensure VM is deployed
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

source .env

# Set initial boot order config
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify EVE received the config
message 'TC10a: Verify initial config received'
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Now change LPS address to a different value (simulating LPS migration)
# This should trigger UpdateLpsConfig() which pauses tasks and re-discovers addresses
message 'TC10b: Changing LPS address (triggers pause/resume)'
exec bash get-app-ip.sh local-manager
source .env

# Update LPS address with a port change (same IP, different representation)
# This triggers the code path with pause() in UpdateLpsConfig()
eden controller edge-node update --device local_profile_server=$app_ip:8888

# Wait for EVE to process the LPS address change
exec sleep 15

# Update the LPS config with new boot order
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid nousb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify EVE received the new config after LPS address change
message 'TC10c: Verify config received after LPS address change'
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Restart VM to apply and verify
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash record-timestamp.sh

message 'TC10d: Verify fw_cfg=nousb applied after address change'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

message '=== TC10 PASSED ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Ensure VM is deployed
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

# Verify EVE received the config (200/201 response)

exec -t 1m bash verify-polling-interval.sh normal
stdout 'Polling interval: normal'

message 'TC11 PASSED: 200/201 response handled correctly'

# --- TC12: HTTP 204 - No Content (no config changes) ---
# LPS returns 204 when the config file ModTime hasn't changed since last request.
# This tests that EVE preserves existing boot order when receiving 204.
message 'TC12: Testing HTTP 204 (no content - config unchanged)'

# Set initial config to usb, wait for EVE to fetch it
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify EVE received the initial config
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Wait for EVE to poll again - LPS will return 204 since file wasn't modified
# (no touch, no content change)
message 'TC12a: Waiting for 204 response (no file modification)'
exec sleep 15

# Verify boot order is still applied correctly after 204
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash record-timestamp.sh

message 'TC12b: Verify fw_cfg=usb preserved after 204 responses'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

message 'TC12c: Verify VM still boots from USB (Debian) - config preserved'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

exec -t 1m bash verify-polling-interval.sh normal
stdout 'Polling interval: normal'

message 'TC12d: Testing HTTP 200 with same content (should behave like 204)'

# Touch the file to update ModTime - LPS will return 200 with same content
exec -t 1m bash touch-lps-config.sh

# Wait for EVE to poll and receive 200 with same content
exec sleep 15

# Verify boot order is still applied correctly (EVE detected no change)
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash record-timestamp.sh

message 'TC12e: Verify fw_cfg=usb preserved after 200 with same content'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

message 'TC12f: Verify VM still boots from USB (Debian)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

message 'TC12 PASSED: 204 and 200-with-same-content preserve boot order'

# --- TC13: HTTP 404 - Not Found (triggers throttling) ---
message 'TC13: Testing HTTP 404 (not found - triggers throttle)'

# Remove the config file to trigger 404 response
exec -t 1m bash trigger-lps-404.sh

# Wait for EVE to poll and receive 404
exec sleep 15

# Verify EVE switched to throttled polling (5 minute interval)
exec -t 1m bash verify-polling-interval.sh throttled
stdout 'Polling interval: throttled'

# Restore config file and verify EVE recovers
message 'TC13a: Verify recovery from 404 throttle'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid nousb

# Need to wait for throttle period or trigger immediate fetch
# The TriggerAppBootConfigGET is called when LPS config changes
eden controller edge-node update --device local_profile_server=$app_ip:8888
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify EVE received config and is back to normal polling
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

exec -t 1m bash verify-polling-interval.sh normal
stdout 'Polling interval: normal'

message 'TC13 PASSED: 404 throttle and recovery work correctly'

message '=== TC11-13 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC17: Persistence - Verify boot config persists across EVE reboot
# This tests that saveAppBootConfig/loadSavedAppBootConfig work correctly
#
# We use nousb with NO custom resolution to properly test:
# - Without nousb and without resolution: VM would boot from USB (Debian) by default
# - With nousb: VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) regardless of resolution
# - After reboot: nousb should persist, so VM still boots from HDD (Ubuntu)
#
# NOTE: Requires TPM to be DISABLED in Eden config (eve.tpm = false) to avoid
# vcomlink startup issues after reboot.
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC17: Config persists across EVE reboot ==='

# Clean LPS state before test
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Explicitly clear custom resolution so OVMF would default to USB boot
# This makes the nousb setting the only thing preventing USB boot
eden controller edge-node update --config app.fml.resolution=

# Delete existing VMs to start fresh for reboot test
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm_2"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm_2"}}

# Deploy fresh VM for reboot test
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

# First verify VM boots from USB (Debian) by default (no resolution, no fw_cfg)
# This confirms that without nousb, USB boot is the default
exec bash record-timestamp.sh
message 'TC17a: Verify VM boots from USB (Debian) by default (no resolution set)'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} debian
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Step 1: Set boot order to nousb via LPS
# Without this, VM would boot from USB (Debian) since no resolution is set
message 'TC17b: Set boot order to nousb (without resolution, USB would be default)'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid nousb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify config is applied
exec -t 2m bash verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'EVE received boot order config'

# Restart VM to apply nousb setting
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash record-timestamp.sh
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

message 'TC17c: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) after applying nousb'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

# Step 2: Reboot EVE via controller (proper way in Eden tests)
# Using eden.reboot.test which triggers reboot by incrementing reboot counter
message 'TC17d: Triggering EVE reboot via controller...'
test eden.reboot.test -test.v -timewait=10m -reboot=1 -count=1 &

# Wait for VM to go HALTED during reboot
message 'TC17e: Waiting for VM to halt during reboot...'
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}

# Wait for VM to be running again after EVE reboot
message 'TC17f: Waiting for VM to be running after EVE reboot...'
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m -check-new RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Step 3: Verify config persisted - check fw_cfg is still nousb
message 'TC17g: Verify fw_cfg=nousb persisted after EVE reboot'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid nousb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: nousb'

# Step 4: Verify VM boots from HDD (proves nousb config was restored from disk)
# If config didn't persist, VM would boot from USB (Debian) since no resolution is set
message 'TC17h: Verify VM boots from HDD (Ubuntu) after EVE reboot'
exec -t 2m bash verify-boot-os-v2.sh {{template "test_vm"}} ubuntu
stdout 'BOOT OS VERIFIED'

message '=== TC17 PASSED ==='

# ============================================================================
# TC18: Warning when setting boot order on running VM
# When boot order is changed for a running VM, EVE should:
# 1. Store the new config (applied on next restart)
# 2. Log a WARNING to indicate restart is needed
# 3. The warning should include "restart required to apply"
# 4. After restart, the warning should be cleared
#
# NOTE: The warning is visible in EVE logs but may be transient in controller
# info messages because it can be cleared by subsequent status updates before
# the next info message is sent to the controller.
#
# CLEAN SETUP: This test starts fresh by:
# - Cleaning LPS state (empty config)
# - Deleting any existing VM
# - Deploying a fresh VM with a new UUID
# - Recording timestamp before action for log filtering
#
# VERIFICATION: verify-boot-order-warning.sh checks:
# 1. App instance status file (most reliable - warning is stored here)
# 2. EVE logs filtered by VM UUID
# 3. Fallback: recent logs with boot order indicators
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC18: Warning when setting boot order on running VM ==='

# After EVE reboot in TC17, ensure local-manager (LPS) is properly running
# The local-manager container restarts after EVE reboot, but process may need restart
message 'TC18: Verifying local-manager is accessible after EVE reboot'
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m RUNNING local-manager
exec -t 5m bash wait-ssh.sh {{template "port"}}
exec -t 1m bash local-manager-start.sh
exec -t 2m bash verify-lps-endpoint.sh
! stdout 'ENDPOINT_ERROR'
stdout 'LPS endpoint verified'

# Clean LPS state before test - ensures no leftover boot order config
exec -t 1m bash clean-lps-state.sh

# Delete existing VM from previous test (if exists) - ensures fresh UUID
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

# Deploy a fresh VM for this test
eden pod deploy -n {{template "test_vm"}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 --fml -p {{template "vm_port"}}:22 --adapters $usb_adapter https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img --networks={{template "network"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash get-vm-uuid.sh {{template "test_vm"}}
source .env

exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Set boot order while VM is running - this should produce a warning
message 'TC18a: Set boot order on running VM (should produce warning in EVE logs)'
exec -t 2m bash set-vm-boot-order.sh $vm_uuid usb
exec -t 2m bash wait-vm-config-applied.sh

# Verify warning appears in EVE logs
message 'TC18b: Verify warning message in EVE logs'
exec -t 1m bash verify-boot-order-warning.sh $vm_uuid
stdout 'WARNING: Boot order change detected in EVE'

# Verify VM is still running (not crashed/stopped)
message 'TC18c: Verify VM is still running after boot order change'
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 1m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

# Restart VM and verify warning clears and config is applied
message 'TC18d: Restart VM to apply boot order'
eden pod stop {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m HALTED {{template "test_vm"}}
eden pod start {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m RUNNING {{template "test_vm"}}

exec bash record-timestamp.sh

# Verify fw_cfg is now applied
message 'TC18e: Verify fw_cfg=usb after restart'
exec -t 2m bash verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh $vm_uuid usb
stdout 'fw_cfg USB boot: usb'

# Verify warning is cleared after restart (no active warning in EVE status)
message 'TC18f: Verify warning is cleared after restart'
exec -t 1m bash verify-no-boot-order-warning.sh $vm_uuid
stdout 'No active boot order warning'

# Clean up for next test
eden pod delete {{template "test_vm"}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 5m - {{template "test_vm"}}

message '=== TC18 PASSED ==='

message 'CLEANUP: Removing test VMs and local-manager'

test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 15m - {{template "test_vm"}}

test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 15m - {{template "test_vm_2"}}
eden pod delete local-manager
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 15m - local-manager
eden network delete {{template "network"}}
test eden.network.test -test.v -timewait 10m - {{template "network"}}

message '=== ALL TESTS PASSED ==='

-- wait-ssh.sh --
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
for p in $*
do
  for i in $(seq 20)
  do
    sleep 20
    # Test SSH-access to container
    echo $EDEN sdn fwd eth0 $p -- {{template "ssh"}} grep -q Ubuntu /etc/issue
    $EDEN sdn fwd eth0 $p -- {{template "ssh"}} grep -q Ubuntu /etc/issue && break
  done
done

-- wait-for-running-once.sh --
# Wait for a pod to reach RUNNING state at least once
# This is useful for VMs that boot briefly and then crash (e.g., USB boot test)
# $1 = pod name
# Polls every 2 seconds for up to 60 attempts (2 minutes)
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
POD_NAME=$1

echo "=== Waiting for pod '$POD_NAME' to reach RUNNING state ==="
echo "Polling every 2 seconds..."

for i in $(seq 120); do
    # Get current state from eden pod ps
    # Use exact match with whitespace after pod name to avoid matching similar names
    # (e.g., test-usb-boot-vm should not match test-usb-boot-vm-2)
    STATE=$($EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^${POD_NAME}[[:space:]]" | awk '{print $NF}')

    echo "Attempt $i/120: Pod '$POD_NAME' state: ${STATE:-not found}"

    if [ "$STATE" = "RUNNING" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: Pod '$POD_NAME' reached RUNNING state!"
        echo "Pod was RUNNING at attempt $i"
        exit 0
    fi

    # Also check if it was RUNNING but already moved to another state
    # by looking at the LAST_STATE column (second to last)
    LAST_STATE=$($EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^${POD_NAME}[[:space:]]" | awk '{print $(NF-1)}')
    if [ "$LAST_STATE" = "RUNNING" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: Pod '$POD_NAME' was RUNNING (now: $STATE)"
        exit 0
    fi

    sleep 2
done

echo "ERROR: Pod '$POD_NAME' never reached RUNNING state after 60 attempts"
echo "Final state: $STATE"
exit 1

EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
ARGS="--token={{template "token"}}"
ARGS="$ARGS --appbootconfig={{template "appbootconfig_file"}}"
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "/root/local_manager $ARGS &>/proc/1/fd/1 &"

-- clean-lps-state.sh --
# Clean LPS state to return default (empty) state for all apps
# This ensures each test starts with a clean slate
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
USB_FILE="{{template "appbootconfig_file"}}"

echo "=== Cleaning LPS state ==="

# Write empty apps config - this is the default state
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "echo '{\"apps\":[]}' > $USB_FILE"

# Verify the file was written
CONTENT=$($EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "cat $USB_FILE" 2>&1)
echo "LPS state reset. Current config: $CONTENT"

# Wait a bit for EVE to pick up the change
echo "Waiting for EVE to process the clean state..."
sleep 10
echo "LPS state cleaned successfully"

-- verify-lps-endpoint.sh --
# Verify that the app boot config endpoint is accessible and returns proper responses
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}

# Create a test config file with empty apps using simple echo

$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "echo '{\"app_configs\":[]}' > $USB_FILE"

# Verify file was created

    echo "ENDPOINT_ERROR: Failed to create app boot config file"

    echo "ENDPOINT_ERROR: local_manager process is not running"
    exit 1
fi

echo "DEBUG: local_manager process is running"
echo ""
echo "LPS endpoint verified: /api/v1/app-boot-config is accessible and functional"
echo "LPS endpoint verified successfully"

-- get-vm-uuid.sh --
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
# Use awk for exact match on pod name (first column) to avoid matching substrings
# e.g., "test-usb-boot-vm" should not match "test-usb-boot-vm-2"
UUID=$($EDEN pod ps | awk -v name="$1" '$1 == name {print $3}')
# Update vm_uuid in .env without losing other variables
if [ -f .env ]; then
    grep -v "^vm_uuid=" .env > .env.tmp 2>/dev/null || true
    mv .env.tmp .env 2>/dev/null || true
fi
echo "vm_uuid=$UUID" >> .env

-- get-vm-uuid-as.sh --
# Get VM UUID and save it with a specific variable name
# Usage: get-vm-uuid-as.sh <vm_name> <variable_name>
# Example: get-vm-uuid-as.sh test-usb-boot-vm vm1_uuid
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_NAME="$1"
VAR_NAME="$2"
# Use awk for exact match on pod name (first column) to avoid matching substrings
UUID=$($EDEN pod ps | awk -v name="$VM_NAME" '$1 == name {print $3}')
# Update variable in .env without losing other variables
if [ -f .env ]; then
    grep -v "^${VAR_NAME}=" .env > .env.tmp 2>/dev/null || true
    mv .env.tmp .env 2>/dev/null || true
fi
echo "${VAR_NAME}=${UUID}" >> .env
echo "Saved ${VAR_NAME}=${UUID}"

-- save-env.sh --
# Save a variable to .env file (update if exists, append if not)
# Usage: save-env.sh <variable_name> <value>
VAR_NAME="$1"
shift
# Join all remaining arguments with space to handle values that might contain spaces
VALUE="$*"
if [ -f .env ]; then
    grep -v "^${VAR_NAME}=" .env > .env.tmp 2>/dev/null || true
    mv .env.tmp .env 2>/dev/null || true
fi
echo "${VAR_NAME}=${VALUE}" >> .env

-- record-timestamp.sh --
# Record current timestamp to .env for log filtering
# Format: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for comparison with eden pod logs timestamps
TS=$(date -u "+%Y%m%d%H%M%S")
TS_READABLE=$(date -u "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

# Remove any existing timestamp entries from .env, then add new ones
if [ -f .env ]; then
    grep -v "^log_start_ts=" .env | grep -v "^log_start_readable=" > .env.tmp 2>/dev/null || true
    mv .env.tmp .env 2>/dev/null || true
fi
echo "log_start_ts=$TS" >> .env
echo "log_start_readable='$TS_READABLE'" >> .env
echo "Recorded timestamp: $TS_READABLE UTC"

-- detect-usb-harddrive.sh --
# Detect USB harddrive on EVE for passthrough to VM
# Uses spec.sh -u to get the USB address for device passthrough
# The address format is: USB<bus>:<port> e.g., USB2:1
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}

echo "=== Detecting USB Harddrive on EVE ==="

# Get spec.sh -u output from EVE which shows USB devices with correct addresses
SPEC_OUTPUT=$($EDEN eve ssh "spec.sh -u" 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:")
echo "Device spec from EVE:"
echo "$SPEC_OUTPUT"
echo ""

# Look for USB device with QEMU USB HARDDRIVE (vendor 46f4, product 0001)
# Extract usbaddr from the JSON output - format: "usbaddr": "2:1"
USB_ADDR=$(echo "$SPEC_OUTPUT" | grep -B2 -A2 '"usbproduct"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"46f4:0001"' | grep -o '"usbaddr"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*"usbaddr"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/')

if [ -z "$USB_ADDR" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: No USB harddrive found in EVE spec"
    echo "Expected: USB device with vendor:product 46f4:0001"
    echo ""
    echo "Available USB devices in spec:"
    echo "$SPEC_OUTPUT" | grep -A10 "IO_TYPE_USB"
    exit 1
fi

# Format as USB<bus>:<port> - the usbaddr is already in format "bus:port" like "2:1"
USB_ADAPTER="USB${USB_ADDR}"

echo "Found USB harddrive address: $USB_ADDR"
echo "USB adapter for passthrough: $USB_ADAPTER"
echo ""

# Save to environment - use USB<addr> format for --adapters flag
echo "usb_adapter=$USB_ADAPTER" >> .env
echo "USB_ADAPTER=$USB_ADAPTER"

-- set-vm-boot-order.sh --
# Set bootOrderConfig for a VM via LPS
# $1 = VM UUID
# $2 = boot order: "usb", "nousb", or "" (empty for default)
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_UUID=$1
BOOT_ORDER=$2
USB_FILE="{{template "appbootconfig_file"}}"

echo "=== Setting bootOrderConfig for VM $VM_UUID to '$BOOT_ORDER' ==="

# Show current config
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "echo '=== Current config ==='; cat $USB_FILE 2>/dev/null || echo 'No file yet'"

# Write the JSON config with usb_boot
# The new format uses usb_boot field in app_configs array
if [ -z "$BOOT_ORDER" ]; then
    # Empty boot order - don't include the field
    JSON="{\"app_configs\":[{\"id\":\"$VM_UUID\",\"displayname\":\"test-usb-boot-vm\"}]}"
else
    JSON="{\"app_configs\":[{\"id\":\"$VM_UUID\",\"displayname\":\"test-usb-boot-vm\",\"usb_boot\":\"$BOOT_ORDER\"}]}"
fi

$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "echo '$JSON' > $USB_FILE && touch $USB_FILE"

# Verify the write
echo "=== New config ==="
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "cat $USB_FILE"
echo ""
echo "VM config updated for $VM_UUID with bootOrderConfig='$BOOT_ORDER'"

-- set-multi-vm-boot-order.sh --
# Set bootOrderConfig for multiple VMs
# $1 = VM1 UUID, $2 = VM1 boot order
# $3 = VM2 UUID, $4 = VM2 boot order
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM1_UUID=$1
VM1_ORDER=$2
VM2_UUID=$3
VM2_ORDER=$4
USB_FILE="{{template "appbootconfig_file"}}"

echo "=== Setting bootOrderConfig for VM1=$VM1_UUID ($VM1_ORDER) and VM2=$VM2_UUID ($VM2_ORDER) ==="

# Build JSON with usb_boot for both VMs
JSON="{\"app_configs\":["
JSON="$JSON{\"id\":\"$VM1_UUID\",\"displayname\":\"test-usb-boot-vm\",\"usb_boot\":\"$VM1_ORDER\"},"
JSON="$JSON{\"id\":\"$VM2_UUID\",\"displayname\":\"test-usb-boot-vm-2\",\"usb_boot\":\"$VM2_ORDER\"}"
JSON="$JSON]}"

$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "echo '$JSON' > $USB_FILE && touch $USB_FILE"

# Verify the write
echo "=== Config file content ==="
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "cat $USB_FILE"
echo ""
echo "Boot order updated: VM1=$VM1_ORDER, VM2=$VM2_ORDER"

# Write JSON config with ONLY id (UUID), NO displayname field
