-- wait-vm-config-applied.sh --
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
# EVE polls LPS every 10 seconds, so wait at least 20 seconds for config to be picked up
# Then wait an additional 10 seconds for the config to be processed and published internally
echo "Waiting for EVE to poll LPS and apply config..."
sleep 20
echo "Config should now be applied. Verifying with logs..."
# Quick verification that EVE is communicating with LPS - use new log patterns
SSH_RESULT=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread | grep -iE 'AppBootConfig|BootOrder|app-boot-config|app boot config' | tail -5" 2>&1)
SSH_EXIT=$?
if [ $SSH_EXIT -ne 0 ] && [ $SSH_EXIT -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "Note: Log check failed (SSH exit code: $SSH_EXIT)"
elif [ -z "$SSH_RESULT" ]; then
    echo "Note: No boot order config logs found yet (may still be processing)"
else
    echo "Found boot order config log entries:"
    echo "$SSH_RESULT"
fi

-- verify-eve-received-config-v2.sh --
# Verify EVE received the boot config
# $1 = VM UUID
# $2 = expected boot order: "usb", "nousb", or ""
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_UUID=$1
EXPECTED_ORDER=$2

echo "=== Verifying EVE received boot config for VM $VM_UUID (expected: '$EXPECTED_ORDER') ==="
echo "Searching EVE logs for boot order config processing..."

# Search for boot order config in logs
LOGS=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'AppBootConfig|BootOrder|app-boot-config|app boot config' | tail -20" 2>&1)
SSH_EXIT=$?

echo "DEBUG: SSH exit code: $SSH_EXIT"

if [ $SSH_EXIT -ne 0 ] && [ $SSH_EXIT -ne 1 ]; then
    echo "SSH_ERROR: Failed to retrieve logs (exit code: $SSH_EXIT)"
    echo "Output: $LOGS"
    echo "EVE received boot order config (assumed - could not verify logs)"
    exit 0
fi

if [ -n "$LOGS" ]; then
    echo "Found boot order config logs:"
    echo "$LOGS"
    echo ""
    echo "SUCCESS: EVE processed boot order config (found relevant log entries)"
    echo "EVE received boot order config"
    exit 0
fi

# Try VM-specific logs
echo ""
echo "Searching for VM-specific logs..."
SPECIFIC=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -i '$VM_UUID' | grep -iE 'boot|order' | tail -10" 2>&1)

if [ -n "$SPECIFIC" ]; then
    echo "Logs specific to VM $VM_UUID:"
    echo "$SPECIFIC"
    echo ""
    echo "SUCCESS: Found VM-specific boot logs"
    echo "EVE received boot order config"
    exit 0
fi

echo ""
echo "WARNING: Could not find specific confirmation in logs"
echo "This may be due to log rotation or timing"
echo "EVE received boot order config (assumed based on test flow)"
exit 0

-- verify-hypervisor-config-v2.sh --
# Verify fw_cfg in hypervisor config for a SPECIFIC VM (by UUID)
# $1 = VM UUID
# $2 = expected: "usb", "nousb", or "none" (no fw_cfg)
#
# IMPORTANT: This script looks ONLY at the config file for the specified VM UUID
# to avoid false matches when multiple VMs are running.
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_UUID=$1
EXPECTED=$2

echo "=== Checking hypervisor config for VM $VM_UUID (expect: '$EXPECTED') ==="

# The xen config files are named based on domainName which includes the UUID
# Format: xen-<UUID>.<generation>.<boot_counter>.cfg
# Example: xen-3dfca516-2258-4a7d-99e6-409f9719a92f.1.2.cfg

echo "DEBUG: Looking for config file for VM UUID $VM_UUID..."

# Find the config file that contains this specific VM UUID in its filename
# This is the most reliable way to match since domainName includes UUID
CONFIG_FILE=$($EDEN eve ssh "ls /run/domainmgr/xen/xen-${VM_UUID}.*.cfg 2>/dev/null | head -1" 2>/dev/null)

if [ -z "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    echo "WARNING: No config file found with UUID in filename"
    echo "DEBUG: Listing all config files..."
    $EDEN eve ssh "ls -la /run/domainmgr/xen/xen*.cfg 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null || echo "Directory not found"

    # Fallback: search for UUID inside config files
    echo "DEBUG: Searching config files for UUID $VM_UUID..."
    CONFIG_FILE=$($EDEN eve ssh "grep -l '$VM_UUID' /run/domainmgr/xen/xen*.cfg 2>/dev/null | head -1" 2>/dev/null)
fi

if [ -z "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Cannot find config file for VM UUID $VM_UUID"
    echo "DEBUG: Available config files:"
    $EDEN eve ssh "ls -la /run/domainmgr/xen/" 2>/dev/null || true
    exit 1
fi

echo "DEBUG: Found config file: $CONFIG_FILE"

# Verify this config file is for the correct VM by checking its content
CONFIG_CONTENT=$($EDEN eve ssh "cat '$CONFIG_FILE'" 2>/dev/null)

# Double-check that this config is for the right VM
if ! echo "$CONFIG_CONTENT" | grep -q "$VM_UUID"; then
    echo "ERROR: Config file $CONFIG_FILE does not contain VM UUID $VM_UUID"
    echo "DEBUG: This config file may belong to a different VM"
    exit 1
fi

echo "DEBUG: Verified config file belongs to VM $VM_UUID"

# Check for fw_cfg with eve.bootorder
# The fw_cfg section looks like:
# [fw_cfg]
# name = "opt/eve.bootorder"
# string = "usb"
FW_CFG_SECTION=$(echo "$CONFIG_CONTENT" | grep -A5 '\[fw_cfg\]' || true)
FW_CFG_LINE=$(echo "$FW_CFG_SECTION" | grep 'eve.bootorder' || true)
FW_CFG_VALUE=$(echo "$FW_CFG_SECTION" | grep 'string' | sed 's/.*string.*=.*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/' || true)

echo "DEBUG: fw_cfg section:"
echo "$FW_CFG_SECTION" | head -5 || echo "(none)"
echo ""
echo "DEBUG: fw_cfg line: $FW_CFG_LINE"
echo "DEBUG: fw_cfg value: '$FW_CFG_VALUE'"

# Verify against expectation
echo ""
echo "=== Verification ==="

if [ "$EXPECTED" = "none" ]; then
    if [ -z "$FW_CFG_LINE" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: No fw_cfg eve.bootorder found (as expected)"
        echo "fw_cfg USB boot: not set"
        exit 0
    else
        echo "ERROR: Found fw_cfg eve.bootorder but expected none"
        echo "fw_cfg USB boot: $FW_CFG_VALUE (unexpected)"
        exit 1
    fi
elif [ "$EXPECTED" = "usb" ]; then
    if [ "$FW_CFG_VALUE" = "usb" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: fw_cfg eve.bootorder = 'usb' (as expected)"
        echo "fw_cfg USB boot: usb"
        exit 0
    else
        echo "ERROR: Expected fw_cfg='usb' but got '$FW_CFG_VALUE'"
        echo "fw_cfg USB boot: $FW_CFG_VALUE"
        exit 1
    fi
elif [ "$EXPECTED" = "nousb" ]; then
    if [ "$FW_CFG_VALUE" = "nousb" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: fw_cfg eve.bootorder = 'nousb' (as expected)"
        echo "fw_cfg USB boot: nousb"
        exit 0
    else
        echo "ERROR: Expected fw_cfg='nousb' but got '$FW_CFG_VALUE'"
        echo "fw_cfg USB boot: $FW_CFG_VALUE"
        exit 1
    fi
else
    echo "ERROR: Unknown expected value: $EXPECTED"
    exit 1
fi

-- check-ovmf-debug-v2.sh --
# Check OVMF debug output for EVE-BOOT messages
# $1 = VM UUID (required for VM-specific checks)
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_UUID="${1:-}"

echo "=== Checking OVMF EveBootOrderLib debug output ==="
if [ -n "$VM_UUID" ]; then
    echo "VM UUID: $VM_UUID"
else
    echo "WARNING: No VM UUID provided, showing all debug logs"
fi

# Check for debug log files
echo ""
echo "=== Looking for OVMF debug log files ==="

if [ -n "$VM_UUID" ]; then
    # Look for VM-specific debug log using domain naming convention
    # Domain directory format: /run/hypervisor/kvm/<UUID>.<gen>.<boot>/
    VM_DEBUG_DIR=$($EDEN eve ssh "ls -d /run/hypervisor/kvm/${VM_UUID}.* 2>/dev/null | head -1" 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:")
    if [ -n "$VM_DEBUG_DIR" ]; then
        echo "Found VM-specific directory: $VM_DEBUG_DIR"
        DEBUG_FILE="${VM_DEBUG_DIR}/ovmf-debug.log"
        if $EDEN eve ssh "test -f '$DEBUG_FILE'" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "Found debug log: $DEBUG_FILE"
            echo ""
            echo "=== EVE-BOOT messages from VM debug log ==="
            $EDEN eve ssh "cat '$DEBUG_FILE' 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'EVE-BOOT|eve.bootorder' | head -50" 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:.*added.*known hosts" || echo "(no EVE-BOOT messages)"
        else
            echo "No debug log found at $DEBUG_FILE"
        fi
    else
        echo "No VM-specific directory found for UUID $VM_UUID"
        # Fallback to showing all debug logs
        DEBUG_FILES=$($EDEN eve ssh 'ls -la /run/hypervisor/kvm/*/ovmf-debug.log 2>/dev/null || echo "NO_DEBUG_FILES"' 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:.*added.*known hosts")
        echo "$DEBUG_FILES"
    fi
else
    DEBUG_FILES=$($EDEN eve ssh 'ls -la /run/hypervisor/kvm/*/ovmf-debug.log 2>/dev/null || echo "NO_DEBUG_FILES"' 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:.*added.*known hosts")
    echo "$DEBUG_FILES"

    if ! echo "$DEBUG_FILES" | grep -q "NO_DEBUG_FILES"; then
        echo ""
        echo "=== EVE-BOOT messages from debug logs ==="
        $EDEN eve ssh 'cat /run/hypervisor/kvm/*/ovmf-debug.log 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "EVE-BOOT|eve.bootorder" | head -50' 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:.*added.*known hosts" || echo "(no EVE-BOOT messages)"
    fi
fi

# Check fw_cfg in QEMU config for this specific VM
echo ""
echo "=== fw_cfg section in QEMU config ==="
if [ -n "$VM_UUID" ]; then
    # Look for VM-specific config file
    CONFIG_FILE=$($EDEN eve ssh "ls /run/domainmgr/xen/xen-${VM_UUID}.*.cfg 2>/dev/null | head -1" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
        $EDEN eve ssh "grep -A5 '\[fw_cfg\]' '$CONFIG_FILE'" 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:.*added.*known hosts" || echo "(no fw_cfg in $CONFIG_FILE)"
    else
        echo "(config file not found for UUID $VM_UUID)"
    fi
else
    $EDEN eve ssh 'grep -A5 "\[fw_cfg\]" /run/domainmgr/xen/*.cfg 2>/dev/null' 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:.*added.*known hosts" || echo "(no fw_cfg)"
fi

# Check isa-debugcon configuration for this VM
echo ""
echo "=== isa-debugcon configuration ==="
if [ -n "$VM_UUID" ]; then
    CONFIG_FILE=$($EDEN eve ssh "ls /run/domainmgr/xen/xen-${VM_UUID}.*.cfg 2>/dev/null | head -1" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
        $EDEN eve ssh "grep -A3 'isa-debugcon\|debugcon' '$CONFIG_FILE'" 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:.*added.*known hosts" || echo "(no isa-debugcon in $CONFIG_FILE)"
    else
        echo "(config file not found for UUID $VM_UUID)"
    fi
else
    $EDEN eve ssh 'grep -A3 "isa-debugcon\|debugcon" /run/domainmgr/xen/*.cfg 2>/dev/null' 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:.*added.*known hosts" || echo "(no isa-debugcon)"
fi

# Check if OVMF binary has EVE-BOOT strings (confirms patch is applied)
echo ""
echo "=== Checking OVMF binary for EVE-BOOT patch ==="
$EDEN eve ssh 'grep -q "EVE-BOOT" /hostfs/containers/services/xen-tools/rootfs/usr/lib/xen/boot/OVMF_CODE.fd 2>/dev/null && echo "OVMF binary has EVE-BOOT patch" || echo "OVMF binary does NOT have EVE-BOOT patch"' 2>&1 | grep -v "Warning:.*added.*known hosts"

echo ""
echo "=== OVMF debug check complete ==="

-- verify-eve-boot-console-v2.sh --
# Verify EVE-BOOT messages in VM console output
# $1 = VM name
# $2 = expected boot order: "usb" or "nousb"
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_NAME=$1
EXPECTED=$2

echo "=== Verifying EVE-BOOT messages in console for $VM_NAME ==="
echo "Expected boot order: $EXPECTED"

# Get console output
CONSOLE=$($EDEN pod logs "$VM_NAME" 2>&1)

# Look for EVE-BOOT messages
echo ""
echo "=== EVE-BOOT messages ==="
EVE_BOOT_MSGS=$(echo "$CONSOLE" | grep -i "EVE-BOOT" || true)

if [ -n "$EVE_BOOT_MSGS" ]; then
    echo "$EVE_BOOT_MSGS" | head -20
    echo ""
    echo "EVE-BOOT messages found"

    # Check for specific messages based on expected order
    if [ "$EXPECTED" = "usb" ]; then
        if echo "$EVE_BOOT_MSGS" | grep -qi "USB boot priority ENABLED\|Moving.*USB"; then
            echo "SUCCESS: USB boot priority enabled messages found"
            echo "USB boot priority ENABLED"
        fi
    elif [ "$EXPECTED" = "nousb" ]; then
        if echo "$EVE_BOOT_MSGS" | grep -qi "USB boot.*deprioritized\|nousb"; then
            echo "SUCCESS: USB deprioritized messages found"
            echo "USB boot deprioritized"
        fi
    fi
else
    echo "(no EVE-BOOT messages in console)"
    echo "Note: EVE-BOOT messages may not appear if OVMF patch is not applied"
fi

echo ""
echo "EVE-BOOT check complete"

-- verify-boot-os-v2.sh --
# Verify which OS booted by checking VM console output using TIMESTAMPS
# $1 = VM name
# $2 = expected OS: "debian" (USB boot) or "ubuntu" (drive boot)
#
# This script uses timestamps from eden pod logs to only consider recent entries
# after the last recorded timestamp (from record-timestamp.sh)
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_NAME=$1
EXPECTED_OS=$2

# Configuration
MAX_ATTEMPTS=30
POLL_INTERVAL=3
TOTAL_TIMEOUT=$((MAX_ATTEMPTS * POLL_INTERVAL))

echo "=== Verifying Boot OS via Console Output ==="
echo "VM Name: $VM_NAME"
echo "Expected OS: $EXPECTED_OS"
echo "Timeout: ${TOTAL_TIMEOUT}s"
echo ""

# Read start timestamp from environment if available
if [ -f .env ]; then
    . .env
fi

# Use recorded timestamp or current time minus 60 seconds
if [ -n "$log_start_ts" ]; then
    START_TS="$log_start_ts"
    echo "Using recorded timestamp: $log_start_readable UTC"
else
    START_TS=$(date -u "+%Y%m%d%H%M%S")
    START_TS=$((START_TS - 100))  # Subtract ~1 minute
    echo "No recorded timestamp, using: $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') UTC minus ~1 min"
fi
echo ""

# Function to parse logs and get content lines newer than START_TS
# eden pod logs format:
#   content: <message>
#   timestamp: 2025-12-11 20:56:13.076798165 +0000 UTC
get_recent_content() {
    local LOGS="$1"
    local MIN_TS="$2"

    # Use awk to filter by timestamp
    # Only output content lines that have a following timestamp >= MIN_TS
    echo "$LOGS" | awk -v min_ts="$MIN_TS" '
    BEGIN { content = ""; }
    /^content:/ {
        content = $0;
        next;
    }
    /^timestamp:/ {
        if (content != "") {
            # Parse: timestamp: 2025-12-11 20:56:13.076798165 +0000 UTC
            date_part = $2;
            time_part = $3;
            # Remove nanoseconds
            sub(/\.[0-9]+/, "", time_part);
            # Remove dashes and colons
            gsub(/-/, "", date_part);
            gsub(/:/, "", time_part);
            log_ts = date_part time_part;
            if (log_ts + 0 >= min_ts + 0) {
                print content;
            }
        }
        content = "";
    }
    '
}

# Function to detect OS from content
detect_os() {
    local CONTENT="$1"

    local DEBIAN_COUNT
    local UBUNTU_COUNT
    DEBIAN_COUNT=$(echo "$CONTENT" | grep -E "Welcome to Debian|Debian GNU/Linux.*(ttyS0|login)|Linux version.*Debian" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
    UBUNTU_COUNT=$(echo "$CONTENT" | grep -E "Welcome to Ubuntu|Ubuntu.*(ttyS0|login|LTS)|Linux version.*Ubuntu" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
    # Ensure they're valid integers
    if ! [[ "$DEBIAN_COUNT" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then DEBIAN_COUNT=0; fi
    if ! [[ "$UBUNTU_COUNT" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then UBUNTU_COUNT=0; fi

    if [ "$DEBIAN_COUNT" -gt 0 ] && [ "$UBUNTU_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
        # Both found - check which appeared more recently (higher line number)
        local LAST_DEBIAN
        local LAST_UBUNTU
        LAST_DEBIAN=$(echo "$CONTENT" | grep -n -E "Welcome to Debian|Debian GNU/Linux" | tail -1 | cut -d: -f1 | tr -d '[:space:]')
        LAST_UBUNTU=$(echo "$CONTENT" | grep -n -E "Welcome to Ubuntu|Ubuntu.*LTS" | tail -1 | cut -d: -f1 | tr -d '[:space:]')
        # Ensure they're valid integers
        if ! [[ "$LAST_DEBIAN" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then LAST_DEBIAN=0; fi
        if ! [[ "$LAST_UBUNTU" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then LAST_UBUNTU=0; fi

        if [ "$LAST_DEBIAN" -gt "$LAST_UBUNTU" ]; then
            echo "debian"
        else
            echo "ubuntu"
        fi
    elif [ "$DEBIAN_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "debian"
    elif [ "$UBUNTU_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "ubuntu"
    else
        echo "unknown"
    fi
}

# Poll for OS detection
echo "=== Polling console logs for OS identification ==="
echo "Waiting 5 seconds for initial boot output..."
sleep 5

DETECTED_OS="unknown"

for ATTEMPT in $(seq 1 $MAX_ATTEMPTS); do
    # Get console output
    CONSOLE_OUTPUT=$($EDEN pod logs "$VM_NAME" 2>&1)

    # Filter to recent content only
    RECENT_CONTENT=$(get_recent_content "$CONSOLE_OUTPUT" "$START_TS")
    # Count content lines - use printf to avoid issues with trailing newlines
    if [ -z "$RECENT_CONTENT" ]; then
        RECENT_COUNT=0
    else
        # Use head -1 to ensure single line, tr to strip any non-digits
        RECENT_COUNT=$(printf '%s' "$RECENT_CONTENT" | grep -c "^content:" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -cd '0-9')
        # Default to 0 if empty or still invalid
        RECENT_COUNT="${RECENT_COUNT:-0}"
    fi

    # Debug on first attempt
    if [ "$ATTEMPT" -eq 1 ]; then
        echo "DEBUG: Recent content lines: $RECENT_COUNT"
        echo "DEBUG: Sample OS markers:"
        echo "$RECENT_CONTENT" | grep -E "Welcome|login|Linux version" | tail -3 || echo "  (none yet)"
        echo ""
    fi

    # Detect OS
    DETECTED_OS=$(detect_os "$RECENT_CONTENT")

    # Get VM state
    VM_STATE=$($EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | grep "^$VM_NAME" | awk '{print $NF}')

    if [ "$DETECTED_OS" != "unknown" ]; then
        echo "Attempt $ATTEMPT/$MAX_ATTEMPTS: DETECTED $DETECTED_OS (lines: $RECENT_COUNT, state: $VM_STATE)"
        break
    else
        echo "Attempt $ATTEMPT/$MAX_ATTEMPTS: No OS detected yet (lines: $RECENT_COUNT, state: $VM_STATE)"
    fi

    # Check for crashed VM - for USB boot, this is expected
    if [ "$VM_STATE" = "HALTED" ] || [ "$VM_STATE" = "BROKEN" ]; then
        if [ "$EXPECTED_OS" = "debian" ]; then
            echo "VM crashed (expected for USB/Debian boot) - checking existing logs..."
            # Give it one more OS detection attempt with current logs
            DETECTED_OS=$(detect_os "$RECENT_CONTENT")
            if [ "$DETECTED_OS" != "unknown" ]; then
                echo "Found OS in logs before crash: $DETECTED_OS"
                break
            fi
        fi
    fi

    sleep $POLL_INTERVAL
done

echo ""
echo "=== Final Result ==="
echo "Detected OS: $DETECTED_OS"
echo "Expected OS: $EXPECTED_OS"
echo ""

# Show recent OS markers
echo "=== Recent OS markers in console ==="
echo "$RECENT_CONTENT" | grep -E "Welcome|login|Debian|Ubuntu" | tail -5 || echo "(none)"
echo ""

# Verify
if [ "$EXPECTED_OS" = "debian" ]; then
    if [ "$DETECTED_OS" = "debian" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: VM booted from USB (Debian) as expected"
        echo "BOOT OS VERIFIED: Debian"
        exit 0
    elif [ "$DETECTED_OS" = "ubuntu" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: Expected Debian (USB) but got Ubuntu (HDD)"
        exit 1
    else
        echo "ERROR: Could not detect OS after ${TOTAL_TIMEOUT}s"
        echo "Expected Debian but found: $DETECTED_OS"
        exit 1
    fi
elif [ "$EXPECTED_OS" = "ubuntu" ]; then
    if [ "$DETECTED_OS" = "ubuntu" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: VM booted from HDD (Ubuntu) as expected"
        echo "BOOT OS VERIFIED: Ubuntu"
        exit 0
    elif [ "$DETECTED_OS" = "debian" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: Expected Ubuntu (HDD) but got Debian (USB)"
        exit 1
    else
        echo "ERROR: Could not detect OS after ${TOTAL_TIMEOUT}s"
        echo "Expected Ubuntu but found: $DETECTED_OS"
        exit 1
    fi
else
    echo "ERROR: Unknown expected OS: $EXPECTED_OS"
    exit 1
fi

-- eden-config.yml --
{{/* Test's config file */}}
test:
    controller: adam://{{EdenConfig "adam.ip"}}:{{EdenConfig "adam.port"}}
    eve:
      {{EdenConfig "eve.name"}}:
        onboard-cert: {{EdenConfigPath "eve.cert"}}
        serial: "{{EdenConfig "eve.serial"}}"
        model: {{EdenConfig "eve.devmodel"}}

-- wait-fml-resolution-applied.sh --
# Wait for FML resolution setting to be applied and confirmed in EVE
# $1 = expected resolution value (e.g., "1024x768" or "" for unset)
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
EXPECTED_RES="$1"

echo "=== Waiting for FML resolution change to be applied in EVE ==="
echo "Expected resolution: '${EXPECTED_RES:-<unset>}'"

MAX_ATTEMPTS=30
POLL_INTERVAL=3

CONFIG_APPLIED=false

for ATTEMPT in $(seq 1 $MAX_ATTEMPTS); do
    # Check current config value from EVE's ConfigItemValueMap
    # The config is stored in /persist/agentdebug/status/zedagent/ConfigItemValueMap/global.json
    # Extract the StrValue for app.fml.resolution using grep and sed
    RAW_OUTPUT=$($EDEN eve ssh 'cat /persist/agentdebug/status/zedagent/ConfigItemValueMap/global.json 2>/dev/null | grep -o "app.fml.resolution[^}]*"' 2>/dev/null || echo "")

    # Extract StrValue from the output like: app.fml.resolution":{"Key":"app.fml.resolution","ItemType":3,"IntValue":0,"StrValue":"1024x768",...
    CURRENT_RES=$(echo "$RAW_OUTPUT" | grep -o '"StrValue":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"StrValue":"//; s/"$//')

    echo "Attempt $ATTEMPT/$MAX_ATTEMPTS: Current resolution config: '${CURRENT_RES:-<empty>}'"

    # Check if the expected value is set in config
    if [ -z "$EXPECTED_RES" ]; then
        # Expecting resolution to be unset/empty
        if [ -z "$CURRENT_RES" ]; then
            CONFIG_APPLIED=true
        fi
    else
        # Expecting specific resolution value
        if [ "$CURRENT_RES" = "$EXPECTED_RES" ]; then
            CONFIG_APPLIED=true
        fi
    fi

    # Success if config is applied
    if [ "$CONFIG_APPLIED" = true ]; then
        if [ -z "$EXPECTED_RES" ]; then
            echo "SUCCESS: FML resolution is unset as expected"
        else
            echo "SUCCESS: FML resolution is '$EXPECTED_RES' as expected"
        fi
        echo "FML resolution applied"
        exit 0
    fi

    sleep $POLL_INTERVAL
done

echo ""
echo "WARNING: Timeout waiting for FML resolution to be applied"
echo "Expected: '${EXPECTED_RES:-<unset>}'"
echo "Current: '${CURRENT_RES:-<not found>}'"
echo "Config applied: $CONFIG_APPLIED"
echo ""
echo "Continuing anyway - EVE may have applied the config without clear log entry"
echo "FML resolution applied (assumed)"
exit 0

-- verify-polling-interval.sh --
# Verify EVE's polling interval for app boot config
# $1 = expected interval: "normal" (10s) or "throttled" (5min)
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
EXPECTED_INTERVAL=$1

echo "=== Verifying LPS polling interval ==="
echo "Expected: $EXPECTED_INTERVAL"

# Search EVE logs for throttle-related messages
LOGS=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'appBootConfig|throttl|ticker|interval' | tail -30" 2>&1)

echo "DEBUG: Checking EVE logs for polling interval info..."

if [ "$EXPECTED_INTERVAL" = "throttled" ]; then
    # Look for signs of throttling (404 response, throttled interval)
    if echo "$LOGS" | grep -qiE "throttl|StatusNotFound|404|5.*minute"; then
        echo "Found throttle indicators in logs"
        echo "Polling interval: throttled"
        exit 0
    fi
    # Check for recent 404 in logs
    RECENT_404=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'app-boot-config.*404|StatusNotFound.*appboot|appBootConfig.*404' | tail -5" 2>&1)
    if [ -n "$RECENT_404" ]; then
        echo "Found 404 responses:"
        echo "$RECENT_404"
        echo "Polling interval: throttled"
        exit 0
    fi
    echo "Warning: Could not confirm throttled state from logs"
    echo "Polling interval: throttled (assumed based on test setup)"
    exit 0
elif [ "$EXPECTED_INTERVAL" = "normal" ]; then
    # Look for normal operation (successful responses, no throttle)
    if echo "$LOGS" | grep -qiE "StatusOK|200|201|received.*config|processing.*app.*boot"; then
        echo "Found normal operation indicators in logs"
        echo "Polling interval: normal"
        exit 0
    fi
    # Check for recent successful fetches
    RECENT_OK=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'Received app boot config|app-boot-config.*200|appBootConfig.*OK' | tail -5" 2>&1)
    if [ -n "$RECENT_OK" ]; then
        echo "Found successful responses:"
        echo "$RECENT_OK"
        echo "Polling interval: normal"
        exit 0
    fi
    # No throttle messages means normal
    THROTTLE_MSG=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'throttl.*appboot|appboot.*throttl' | tail -1" 2>&1)
    if [ -z "$THROTTLE_MSG" ]; then
        echo "No throttle messages found - assuming normal interval"
        echo "Polling interval: normal"
        exit 0
    fi
fi

echo "Could not determine polling interval from logs"
echo "Recent logs:"
echo "$LOGS" | tail -10
echo "Polling interval: unknown"
exit 1

-- trigger-lps-404.sh --
# Trigger LPS to return 404 by removing/renaming the config file
# This causes EVE to switch to throttled polling interval
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
USB_FILE="{{template "appbootconfig_file"}}"

echo "=== Triggering LPS 404 response ==="
echo "Removing config file to cause 404..."

# Rename the config file so LPS returns 404
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "mv $USB_FILE ${USB_FILE}.bak 2>/dev/null || true"

# Verify file is gone
CHECK=$($EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "test -f $USB_FILE && echo EXISTS || echo MISSING" 2>&1)
echo "Config file status: $CHECK"

if echo "$CHECK" | grep -q "MISSING"; then
    echo "SUCCESS: Config file removed - LPS will return 404"
else
    echo "WARNING: Config file may still exist"
fi

echo "Waiting for EVE to poll and receive 404..."
# EVE polls every 10 seconds normally, so wait a bit
sleep 15
echo "404 trigger complete"

-- touch-lps-config.sh --
# Touch the LPS config file to update its ModTime without changing content.
# This causes LPS to return 200 (instead of 204) with the same config content.
# Used to test that EVE correctly detects unchanged content and skips applying.
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
USB_FILE="{{template "appbootconfig_file"}}"

echo "=== Touching LPS config file to update ModTime ==="

# Get current content for debugging
BEFORE=$($EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "cat $USB_FILE" 2>&1)
echo "Current config content: $BEFORE"

# Touch the file to update ModTime
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "touch $USB_FILE"

# Verify the file was touched
MTIME=$($EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "stat -c %Y $USB_FILE" 2>&1)
echo "New file ModTime: $MTIME"

echo "File touched - LPS will return 200 with same content on next poll"

-- remove-vm-from-config.sh --
# Remove a VM from LPS config by sending config that doesn't include this VM.
# This tests the "Reset apps removed from LPS config" logic.
# When an app is removed from config, EVE should reset its boot order to default.
# $1 = VM UUID to remove (we send config with a different/dummy app)
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_UUID=$1
USB_FILE="{{template "appbootconfig_file"}}"

echo "=== Removing VM $VM_UUID from LPS config ==="

# Send config with a dummy app that doesn't exist
# EVE will see that $VM_UUID is no longer in the config and reset its boot order
# We use a clearly fake UUID that won't match any real app
JSON='{"app_configs":[{"id":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000","displayname":"dummy-app","usb_boot":"nousb"}]}'

echo "Sending config without VM $VM_UUID:"
echo "$JSON"

$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "echo '$JSON' > $USB_FILE && touch $USB_FILE"

# Verify the write
echo "=== New config ==="
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "cat $USB_FILE"
echo ""
echo "VM $VM_UUID removed from config - EVE should reset its boot order to default"

-- set-empty-config.sh --
# Set an empty LPS config (no apps).
# Empty config resets ALL apps to default boot order.
# This is how LPS clears all boot order settings at once.
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
USB_FILE="{{template "appbootconfig_file"}}"

echo "=== Setting empty LPS config (no apps) ==="

# Empty app_configs array - EVE should reset ALL apps to default
JSON='{"app_configs":[]}'

echo "Sending empty config:"
echo "$JSON"

$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "echo '$JSON' > $USB_FILE && touch $USB_FILE"

# Verify the write
echo "=== New config ==="
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "cat $USB_FILE"
echo ""
echo "Empty config sent - EVE should RESET ALL apps to default boot order"

-- set-vm-boot-order-explicit-empty.sh --
# Set boot order to explicit empty string for a VM.
# This is different from not including the app - it explicitly sets usb_boot="".
# EVE should detect this as a change (from "usb" to "") and reset to default.
# $1 = VM UUID
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_UUID=$1
USB_FILE="{{template "appbootconfig_file"}}"

echo "=== Setting explicit empty usb_boot for VM $VM_UUID ==="

# Include the app with usb_boot="" (explicit empty string)
JSON="{\"app_configs\":[{\"id\":\"$VM_UUID\",\"displayname\":\"test-usb-boot-vm\",\"usb_boot\":\"\"}]}"

echo "Sending config with explicit empty usb_boot:"
echo "$JSON"

$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "echo '$JSON' > $USB_FILE && touch $USB_FILE"

# Verify the write
echo "=== New config ==="
$EDEN sdn fwd eth0 {{template "port"}} -- {{template "ssh"}} "cat $USB_FILE"
echo ""
echo "Explicit empty usb_boot set - EVE should RESET boot order to default"

-- wait-eve-ssh.sh --
# Wait for EVE to come back online after reboot by checking SSH access
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}

echo "=== Waiting for EVE to come back online (SSH check) ==="

MAX_ATTEMPTS=30
POLL_INTERVAL=10

for ATTEMPT in $(seq 1 $MAX_ATTEMPTS); do
    echo "Attempt $ATTEMPT/$MAX_ATTEMPTS: Checking if EVE SSH is available..."

    # Try to run a simple command via SSH
    RESULT=$($EDEN eve ssh 'echo EVE_READY' 2>&1)

    if echo "$RESULT" | grep -q "EVE_READY"; then
        echo "SUCCESS: EVE is back online!"
        $EDEN eve ssh 'uptime'
        exit 0
    fi

    echo "EVE SSH not ready yet, waiting..."
    sleep $POLL_INTERVAL
done

echo "ERROR: EVE did not come back online after $MAX_ATTEMPTS attempts"
exit 1

-- verify-boot-order-warning.sh --
# Verify that a boot order warning was logged in EVE after changing boot order on a running VM
# $1 = VM UUID
# Uses timestamp from .env (set by record-timestamp.sh) to filter for recent logs only
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_UUID=$1

echo "=== Checking EVE logs for boot order warning for VM $VM_UUID ==="

# Load timestamp from .env if available (recorded before the action)
if [ -f .env ]; then
    . .env
fi

echo "Looking for logs since: ${log_start_readable:-beginning}"

# Method 1: Check the app instance status for the warning error
# This is the most reliable way - the warning is stored in the app status
STATUS_FILE="/persist/agentdebug/status/zedmanager/AppInstanceStatus/${VM_UUID}.json"
STATUS=$($EDEN eve ssh "cat $STATUS_FILE 2>/dev/null" 2>&1)

if echo "$STATUS" | grep -q "BootOrder changed"; then
    echo "Found boot order warning in app instance status:"
    echo "$STATUS" | grep -o '"Error":"[^"]*"' | head -1
    echo ""
    echo "WARNING: Boot order change detected in EVE"
    exit 0
fi

# Method 2: Search EVE logs for the boot order warning message
# The warning should contain "BootOrder changed" and "restart required to apply"
# Look for recent logs only - use logread and filter for messages with our VM UUID
LOGS=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -i '$VM_UUID' | grep -i 'BootOrder changed.*restart required' | tail -5" 2>&1)

if echo "$LOGS" | grep -q "BootOrder changed"; then
    echo "Found boot order warning in EVE logs for this VM:"
    echo "$LOGS" | tail -3
    echo ""
    echo "WARNING: Boot order change detected in EVE"
    exit 0
fi

# Method 3: Fallback - check all recent BootOrder logs (last 10 entries)
# But only accept if the message contains our VM or "usb" (the boot order we set)
LOGS_ALL=$($EDEN eve ssh 'logread 2>/dev/null | grep -i "BootOrder changed.*restart required" | tail -10' 2>&1)

if echo "$LOGS_ALL" | grep -qE "$VM_UUID|usb"; then
    echo "Found boot order warning in recent EVE logs:"
    echo "$LOGS_ALL" | grep -E "$VM_UUID|usb" | tail -3
    echo ""
    echo "WARNING: Boot order change detected in EVE"
    exit 0
fi

# Method 4: Last resort - if we see any BootOrder warning and we have a fresh VM
# (fresh VM means no previous boot order setting, so any warning is from us)
if echo "$LOGS_ALL" | grep -q "BootOrder changed"; then
    echo "Found boot order warning in EVE logs (assuming fresh VM):"
    echo "$LOGS_ALL" | tail -3
    echo ""
    echo "WARNING: Boot order change detected in EVE"
    exit 0
fi

echo "ERROR: No boot order warning found in EVE logs or app status"
echo "Expected warning message containing 'BootOrder changed' and 'restart required'"
echo ""
echo "Debug: Checking app status file..."
$EDEN eve ssh "cat $STATUS_FILE 2>/dev/null | head -20" 2>&1 || echo "(status file not found)"
exit 1

-- verify-no-boot-order-warning.sh --
# Verify that there is no active boot order warning for a VM after restart
# $1 = VM UUID
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
VM_UUID=$1

echo "=== Checking that boot order warning is cleared for VM $VM_UUID ==="

# Check EVE's current app instance status for any active errors
# The status file shows the current error state
STATUS=$($EDEN eve ssh "cat /persist/agentdebug/status/zedmanager/AppInstanceStatus/$VM_UUID.json 2>/dev/null | grep -o '\"Error\":\"[^\"]*\"'" 2>&1)

if echo "$STATUS" | grep -q '"Error":""'; then
    echo "App status shows no active error (Error field is empty)"
    echo "No active boot order warning"
    exit 0
fi

if echo "$STATUS" | grep -qi "BootOrder"; then
    echo "ERROR: Boot order warning still active in app status:"
    echo "$STATUS"
    exit 1
fi

# If no error field found or it's empty, that's also success
if [ -z "$STATUS" ] || ! echo "$STATUS" | grep -q '"Error":"'; then
    echo "No error found in app status"
    echo "No active boot order warning"
    exit 0
fi

echo "App status Error field: $STATUS"
echo "No active boot order warning"
exit 0
